GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.112.
Run 'copilot update' to check for updates.
Usage: copilot [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

GitHub Copilot CLI - An AI-powered coding assistant.

Start an interactive session to chat with Copilot, or use -p/--prompt for
non-interactive scripting. Copilot can edit files, run shell commands, search
your codebase, and more — all with configurable permissions.

Run `copilot <command> --help` for details on any subcommand.

Commands:
  app          Open the GitHub Copilot app
  login        Authenticate with Copilot
  help         Display help information
  init         Initialize Copilot instructions
  config       Manage configuration settings
  update       Download the latest version
  version      Display version information
  workflow     Run dynamic workflows
  sessions     Manage saved sessions
  memories     Manage memories
  plugin       Manage plugins
  mcp          Manage MCP servers
  skill        Manage skills
  instruction  Inspect instruction sources
  lsp          Inspect language server configuration
  sandbox      Manage command sandboxing
  completion   Generate a shell completion script

Options:
      --acp
          Start as Agent Client Protocol server
      --add-dir <directory>
          Allow file access to a directory and load its .github/skills
          and .github/agents as trusted configuration (can be used
          multiple times). A relative path resolves against the
          session working directory (the --resume/--worktree/-C
          directory), whatever order the options appear in
      --add-github-mcp-tool <tool>
          Add a tool to enable for the GitHub MCP server instead of
          the default CLI subset (can be used multiple times). Use "*"
          for all tools.
      --add-github-mcp-toolset <toolset>
          Add a toolset to enable for the GitHub MCP server in addition
          to the default CLI subset (can be used multiple times). Use
          "default" for the server's default toolsets or "all" for all
          toolsets.
      --additional-mcp-config <json>
          Additional MCP servers configuration as JSON string or file
          path (prefix with @) (can be used multiple times; augments
          config from ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json for this session). A
          relative @ path resolves against the session working
          directory (the --resume/--worktree/-C directory) and a
          leading ~/ expands to your home directory
      --agent <agent>
          Specify a custom agent to use
      --allow-all
          Enable all permissions (equivalent to --allow-all-tools
          --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls)
      --allow-all-mcp-server-instructions
          Include initialization instructions from all MCP servers in
          the system prompt instead of only allowlisted servers
      --allow-all-paths
          Disable file path verification and allow access to any path
      --allow-all-tools
          Allow all tools to run automatically without confirmation.
          Non-interactive mode cannot ask, so it denies tool requests
          that no allow rule (or `--assisted-approval`) approves.
          Run `copilot help environment` for what COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL
          accepts and what exact "true" grants [env: COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=]
      --allow-all-urls
          Allow access to all URLs without confirmation
      --allow-tool [<tools>...]
          Tools the CLI has permission to use; will not prompt for
          permission. Takes rules like 'shell(npm:*)' for every npm
          command or 'write' for all file edits. Rules last for this
          run. Run `copilot help permissions` for the rule syntax
      --allow-url [<urls>...]
          Allow access to specific URLs or domains
      --assisted-approval
          Review tool permission requests with the assisted-approval
          safety judge instead of approving them outright. The judge
          is probabilistic and not a security boundary. Equivalent
          to the `assisted` mode of /permissions. Takes precedence
          over --allow-all-tools when the judge engages. Ignored, with
          a warning, when AUTO_APPROVAL is explicitly disabled or
          managed policy blocks it. (env: COPILOT_ASSISTED_APPROVAL)
      --attachment <path>
          Attach a file (image or native document) to the initial
          prompt; only valid in non-interactive mode (can be used
          multiple times)
      --auto-tier <preference>
          Set the Auto routing profile by its exact advertised ID
          (validated against the available catalog)
      --autopilot
          Start in autopilot mode
      --available-tools [<tools>...]
          Only these tools will be available to the model
      --banner
          Show the startup banner
      --bash-env [<value>]
          Enable BASH_ENV support for bash shells (on|off)
  -C <directory>
          Change working directory before doing anything else
      --connect [<sessionId>]
          Connect directly to a remote session (optionally specify
          session ID or task ID)
      --context <tier>
          Set the context window tier (overrides persisted setting) [possible values: default, long_context]
      --continue
          Resume the most recent session
      --deny-tool [<tools>...]
          Tools the CLI does not have permission to use; will not
          prompt for permission. Takes rules like 'shell(git push)'
          or 'write(.env)'. Deny rules win over every allow, even
          --allow-all and --yolo. Run `copilot help permissions`
          for the rule syntax
      --deny-url [<urls>...]
          Deny access to specific URLs or domains, takes precedence
          over --allow-url
      --disable-builtin-mcps
          Disable all built-in MCP servers (currently:
          github-mcp-server, githubiq)
      --disable-client-telemetry
          Disable Copilot-owned GitHub and Entra telemetry
          (does not affect OpenTelemetry or server-side telemetry)
      --disable-mcp-server <server-name>
          Disable a specific MCP server (can be used multiple times)
      --disallow-temp-dir
          Prevent automatic access to the system temporary directory (and your /tmp files on macOS)
      --dynamic-retrieval <category=on|off>
          Enable or disable embeddings-based dynamic retrieval per
          category and persist the choice (category: skills).
          Repeatable, e.g. --dynamic-retrieval skills=off
      --enable-all-github-mcp-tools
          Enable all GitHub MCP server tools instead of the default
          CLI subset. Overrides --add-github-mcp-toolset and
          --add-github-mcp-tool options.
      --enable-mcp-server <server-name>
          Enable an MCP server disabled in settings for this run only;
          nothing is persisted (can be used multiple times)
      --enable-memory
          Enable memory in prompt mode (disabled by default)
      --excluded-tools [<tools>...]
          These tools will not be available to the model
      --experimental
          Enable experimental features
      --extension-sdk-path <directory>
          Override the bundled @github/copilot-sdk injected into
          extension subprocesses with a local `copilot-sdk/` folder.
          Invalid paths fall back to the bundled SDK.
      --fleet
          Run the prompt in fleet mode (parallel subagent
          orchestration); combine with -i, -p, or piped stdin
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -i, --interactive <prompt>
          Start interactive mode and automatically execute this prompt
      --log-dir <directory>
          Set log file directory (default: ~/.copilot/logs/)
      --log-level <level>
          Set the log level [possible values: none, error, warning, info, debug, all, default]
      --max-ai-credits <credits>
          Set max AI credits for this session
      --max-autopilot-continues <count>
          Maximum number of continuation messages in autopilot mode [default: 5]
      --mcp-github-auth <server=origin>
          Send the signed-in GitHub account credential only to this
          explicit --additional-mcp-config server and approved origin.
          HTTPS is required except for literal loopback HTTP. Never
          put a token in this argument. Can be used multiple times.
      --mode <mode>
          Set the initial agent mode [possible values: interactive, plan, autopilot]
      --model <model>
          Set the AI model to use (use 'auto' to let Copilot pick
          automatically)
      --mouse [<value>]
          Enable mouse support in alt screen mode (on|off)
  -n, --name <name>
          Set a name for the new session
      --no-ask-user
          Disable the ask_user tool (the agent can still ask in its
          replies, but not through the question form)
      --no-auto-update
          Disable downloading CLI updates automatically. Copilot then
          runs the version bundled in the executable you launched
          rather than a newer previously downloaded one
      --no-bash-env
          Disable BASH_ENV support for bash shells
      --no-color
          Disable all color output
      --no-custom-instructions
          Disable loading of custom instructions from AGENTS.md and
          related files
      --no-eager-powershell-resolution
          Disable background PowerShell prompt resolution on Windows
      --no-experimental
          Disable experimental features
      --no-mouse
          Disable mouse support in alt screen mode
      --output-format <format>
          Output format: 'text' (default) or 'json' (JSONL, one JSON
          object per line) [possible values: text, json]
      --plan
          Start in plan mode (combine with --mode autopilot to
          auto-approve the plan and implement it autonomously)
      --plugin-dir <directory>
          Load a plugin from a local directory (can be used multiple
          times). A relative path resolves against the session working
          directory (the --resume/--worktree/-C directory), whatever
          order the options appear in
  -p, --prompt <text>
          Execute a prompt in non-interactive mode (exits after
          completion)
      --reasoning-effort <level>
          Set the reasoning effort level; supported levels depend on the model [possible values: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
  -r, --resume [<value>]
          Resume from a previous session (optionally specify existing
          session ID, task ID, ID prefix, or name; name matching is
          exact, case-insensitive)
      --screen-reader
          Enable screen reader optimizations
      --secret-env-vars [<vars>...]
          Environment variable names to remove from shell and MCP
          server environments. Their values are also masked in some
          output, such as --output-format json, but a value that
          reaches a tool result another way still goes to the model
          and is saved in the session history
          (e.g., --secret-env-vars=MY_KEY,OTHER_KEY)
      --session-id <id>
          Resume an existing session or task by ID, or set the UUID
          for a new session
      --share [<path>]
          Share session to markdown file after completion in
          non-interactive mode (default: ./copilot-session-<id>.md)
      --share-gist
          Share session to a secret GitHub gist after completion in
          non-interactive mode
  -s, --silent
          Output only the agent response (no stats), useful for
          scripting with -p
      --stream <mode>
          Enable or disable streaming mode [possible values: on, off]
      --sync-session[=<on|off>]
          Enable or disable read-only account history sync for this
          run only (omitted: use configured/default behavior).
          Without a value, enables sync; does not enable incoming control. [possible values: on, off]
      --trust-folder
          Trust the resolved working directory's configuration for
          one new prompt-mode session only (no saved trust or tool,
          path, or URL approvals)
      --usage-output-file <file>
          Write final usage statistics as JSON to the specified file
          when the session ends, also for -p and --silent runs: AI
          credits, premium requests, and input, output, cache and
          reasoning tokens per model and per agent (main and each
          subagent)
  -v, --version
          show version information
      --yolo
          Enable all permissions (equivalent to --allow-all-tools
          --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls)

Help Topics:
  acp              Agent Client Protocol and foreground activity
  billing          AI credit usage
  commands         Interactive Mode Commands
  config           Configuration Settings
  environment      Environment Variables
  extensions       Extensions
  input            Input and Keys
  limits           Session Limits Controls
  logging          Logging
  lsp              Language Servers
  mcp              MCP Servers
  monitoring       Monitoring with OpenTelemetry
  network          Corporate proxies and certificates
  parallel-work    Working in Parallel
  permissions      Permissions
  providers        Models and providers (BYOK)
  providers-env    Provider environment variables (legacy)
  providers-local  Models you bring or run yourself
  sandbox          Command Sandboxing
  sessions         Sessions
  timeline         Timeline and Tool Output

Examples:
  # Start interactive mode
  $ copilot

  # Start interactive mode and automatically execute a prompt
  $ copilot -i "Fix the bug in main.js"

  # Execute a prompt in non-interactive mode (exits after completion)
  $ copilot -p "Fix the bug in main.js" --allow-all-tools

  # Trust this checkout's configuration for one prompt-mode session only
  $ copilot --trust-folder -p "Summarize this project"

  # Enable all permissions with a single flag
  $ copilot -p "Fix the bug in main.js" --allow-all
  $ copilot -p "Fix the bug in main.js" --yolo

  # Start with a specific model
  $ copilot --model gpt-5.6-sol

  # Resume the most recent session
  $ copilot --continue

  # Resume a previous session using session picker
  $ copilot --resume

  # Resume a specific session by ID
  $ copilot --resume=<session-id>

  # Name a new session
  $ copilot --name="my feature"

  # Start a new session with a specific UUID
  $ copilot --session-id=0cb916db-26aa-40f2-86b5-1ba81b225fd2

  # Resume or attach to an existing session or task by ID
  $ copilot --session-id=<session-or-task-id>

  # Resume a session by name
  $ copilot --resume="my feature"

  # Resume a session by ID prefix (7+ hex chars)
  $ copilot --resume=0cb916d

  # Resume with auto-approval
  $ copilot --allow-all-tools --resume

  # Allow access to additional directory
  $ copilot --add-dir /home/user/projects

  # Allow multiple directories
  $ copilot --add-dir ~/workspace --add-dir /tmp

  # Disable path verification (allow access to any path)
  $ copilot --allow-all-paths

  # Allow all git commands except git push
  $ copilot --allow-tool='shell(git:*)' --deny-tool='shell(git push)'

  # Allow all file editing
  $ copilot --allow-tool='write'

  # Allow all but one specific tool from MCP server with name "MyMCP"
  $ copilot --deny-tool='MyMCP(denied_tool)' --allow-tool='MyMCP'

  # Allow GitHub API access (defaults to HTTPS)
  $ copilot --allow-url=github.com

  # Deny access to specific domain over HTTPS
  $ copilot --deny-url=https://malicious-site.com
  $ copilot --deny-url=malicious-site.com

  # Allow all URLs without confirmation
  $ copilot --allow-all-urls

  # Initialize Copilot instructions for a repository
  $ copilot init

Learn More:
  Use `copilot <command> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the documentation at https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli


$ copilot help sessions
Sessions:

  Every conversation is a session with an ID, saved as you work. /session id shows and copies the
  current ID, /session info its details, and /rename names it.

Starting and resuming:

  copilot --name <name>       Start a new session with a name.
  copilot --continue          Resume the most recent session, preferring one from the current
                              branch, repository or directory.
  copilot --resume [value]    Resume by session ID, ID prefix, task ID or name (exact,
                              case-insensitive); with no value, open the session picker.
  /resume [value]             The same inside the CLI; /continue is an alias.

  In the picker, / searches names, first messages, folders and ID prefixes, enter opens, s cycles
  the sort (relevance, last used, created, name), r refreshes, x deletes and esc cancels.
  Relevance groups sessions by this branch, repository, git root and directory. Unnamed sessions
  with no messages are not listed. Signed in, left/right switches between All, Local and Remote;
  Remote lists sessions in your GitHub account, such as ones synced from another machine. Choose
  Local to pull one's history into a new session here.

What carries over on resume:

  A resumed session keeps its conversation, model, agent mode and allow-all state. --model, --mode,
  --plan, --autopilot and --allow-all still apply when given; `defaultMode` and
  `defaultPermissionMode` only affect new sessions.

Where sessions are stored:

  Each local session is a directory, ~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/ (under $COPILOT_HOME
  when set), with its event log (events.jsonl), metadata (workspace.yaml), plan (plan.md), the
  database the agent's sql tool uses (session.db), checkpoints/ and files/. session-store.db indexes
  sessions for search. These files are not encrypted; --secret-env-vars keeps variables out of
  shells, but a value that reaches a tool result is saved in the history.

The session database (session.db):

  Each session has its own SQLite database file, session.db in its session folder, which the agent
  reads and writes with its sql tool. It keeps its to-do list there, in the todos and todo_deps
  tables, and can add tables of its own to track multi-step work. Other sessions do not see it.
  To see what is in it or to use it, ask the agent, for example "show the pending todos" or "track
  this work as todos"; /fleet works through the open ones.

New sessions, forks and rewind:

  /new starts a new session and keeps the current one running in the background; /clear closes it.
  /fork [name] copies the current session into a new one and switches to it. /new worktree and
  /fork worktree do the same in a new git worktree. /undo (or /rewind, or esc twice on an empty
  prompt) restores an earlier turn: "Conversation only" or "Conversation + files". Compaction saves
  a checkpoint; /session checkpoints [n] lists them or shows one.

Sync, sharing and remote control:

  When you are signed in and your account allows it, session history is synced read-only to your
  GitHub account. Set `remoteExport` to false to stop, or pass --sync-session=off (or =on) for one
  run. /share link makes a synced session visible to anyone who can read its repository;
  /share link off stops that. /share file [path] and /share html [path] export the transcript
  (default copilot-session-<id>.md or copilot-session-<id>.html), /share gist makes a secret gist,
  and -p runs take --share and --share-gist. /remote on lets you steer the session from GitHub on
  the web or mobile, /remote off disconnects and /remote show reports status. If remote control is
  not enabled, an organization administrator has to allow it.

Cleaning up and retention:

  Sessions are kept until you delete them; nothing expires them. These commands act on local
  sessions only, and never on the current session or one open in another process:
    /session cleanup                      Show storage used by other sessions, grouped by age.
    /session prune --older-than <days>    Delete older sessions; --dry-run previews and
                                          --include-named also deletes sessions you named.
    /session delete <id> --yes            Delete one session; without --yes it only previews.
    /session delete-all --yes             Delete all other sessions; without --yes it only previews.
  /session delete with no ID deletes the current session and starts a new one. For a synced
  session it asks "Delete local only" or "Delete local and synced data".

  Process logs clean up after themselves: in ~/.copilot/logs/ (or the --log-dir directory), logs
  older than 7 days, and all but the newest 50, are deleted automatically. "Files and
  directories" in copilot help config lists everything else kept under ~/.copilot.


$ copilot help permissions
Permissions:

  Copilot asks before it runs shell commands, edits files, uses paths or URLs outside what is
  allowed, or calls MCP tools, unless a rule or mode already allows the request. Commands it
  recognizes as read-only run without asking.

Approval prompt:

  Yes                                      Allow this request once.
  Yes, and don't ask again for <command> in this repo (or in this directory)
                                           Saved for that repository or directory in
                                           ~/.copilot/permissions-config.json.
  Yes, and approve <command> for the rest of the running session
                                           Offered instead when there is no location to save.
  No, and tell Copilot what to do differently
                                           Deny, optionally with instructions.

  URL prompts can approve a domain for the session or permanently; permanent approvals are added
  to `allowedUrls` in settings.json. A prompt for docs.example.com also offers to approve
  "https://*.example.com" and its subdomains, so other subdomains of the site stop asking
  (not for IP addresses or names like localhost). That subdomain approval is not remembered:
  it is never saved to settings and ends with the running session. /reset-allowed-tools clears
  session approvals, turns off allow-all, and clears saved approvals for the current location.

Tool rules:

  To let Copilot run a command without asking, start it with --allow-tool, such as
  --allow-tool='shell(npm:*)' for every npm command; --deny-tool='shell(git push)' blocks one.
  These rules last for that run. To stop being asked in a repository, answer the approval prompt
  with "Yes, and don't ask again".

  --allow-tool and --deny-tool take a permission pattern of form kind(argument); the argument is
  optional. Deny rules win over every allow, including --allow-all-tools. --available-tools and
  --excluded-tools instead decide which tools the model can see at all.

    shell(command:*?)
        Matches a shell command; with no argument, every shell command. git, gh, npm, pnpm, yarn,
        cargo, go, pip, mvn, gradle, dotnet and similar tools are matched with their subcommand, as
        in "shell(git push)" or "shell(gh pr)". Only the first subcommand is part of the name, so
        "shell(gh pr)" covers "gh pr create --fill" and "shell(gh pr create)" does not.
        Warning: allowing "shell(gh pr)" also allows "gh pr merge" and "gh pr close" without a
        command approval prompt; shell rules cannot allow only "gh pr create".
        The :* suffix matches that command and anything after it: "shell(git:*)" matches
        "git push" but not "gitea". PowerShell commands match by the name as typed, e.g.
        "shell(Get-ChildItem)", which does not cover its aliases.

    write(path?)
        Matches tools that create and modify files. If the path is omitted, matches all such writes. A relative path
        matches by trailing path components, so "write(.env)" matches a file named ".env" in any directory, not only
        the one in the current working directory; use an absolute path such as "write(/path/to/.env)" or a path
        under your home directory such as "write(~/notes/todo.md)" to scope the rule to a single location.

        Paths also accept glob patterns: "*" and "?" match within one path segment and "**" matches across
        directories, so "write(reports/*/output.txt)" matches reports/a/output.txt and "write(reports/**)" matches
        every file under a reports directory. A pattern cannot exclude paths (there is no "!" negation); to exclude
        a path, add a --deny-tool rule for it. A backslash is read as a path separator, not an escape; to match a
        literal "*", "?" or "[", wrap it in brackets, as in "[*]".

        A rule with a path does not apply to shell commands. An unscoped "write" rule (for example
        --allow-tool='write') approves a shell command's redirection of output into a file, but not the command
        itself: a command that is not read-only, such as "touch marker > output.log", still needs its own shell
        rule, such as "shell(touch)", or --allow-all-tools.

    read(path?)
        Matches file-read requests from built-in tools. If the path is omitted, matches all such reads. Paths match
        the same way as write(path?), so "read(.env)" matches a file named ".env" in any directory.

    memory
        Matches requests to store a memory.

    <mcp-server-name>(tool-name?)
        One tool of an MCP server, or all of its tools, e.g. "MyMCP(my_tool)".

    url(domain-or-url?)
        URL access by the shell and web-fetch tools, e.g. "url(https://*.github.com)".

Paths and URLs:

  File access is limited to the working directory and the system temp directory. --add-dir (or
  /add-dir) adds a directory, --allow-all-paths removes the check, and --disallow-temp-dir drops the
  temp directory. On macOS, your own files under /tmp are allowed too, unless --disallow-temp-dir is
  set. --allow-url, --deny-url and `allowedUrls` are protocol-aware and default to
  https://, so https://example.com does not allow http://example.com. --allow-all-urls allows all.

Allow-all and autopilot:

  --allow-all and --yolo equal --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls. In a session,
  /allow-all (or /permissions allow-all) turns it on and /permissions manual turns it off.
  Even in allow-all (yolo) mode, Copilot still prompts or denies in these cases:

    - --deny-tool rules still deny.
    - A command that asks to run outside the sandbox always prompts.
    - Organization rules (`permissions.deny`, `permissions.ask`, `permissions.allow`) still apply,
      and "ask" rules always prompt. They come only from organization policy, not your settings.json.
    - `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` set to "disable" turns allow-all off.

  In autopilot and -p runs, a tool permission request that would prompt is denied.
  Use --allow-all or --allow-tool rules for unattended work.

  When the agent would ask you a question in autopilot, Copilot answers for you that you are not
  available and will review the work later. The agent then makes its best guess and keeps going,
  or, if the request is genuinely ambiguous, ends the task with a summary of what is unclear. The
  timeline shows the question with "Making best guess".

  MCP input and consent requests that reach the interactive UI, including URL prompts, wait for
  your explicit answer without leaving Autopilot. Pre-approved MCP requests keep their existing
  approval policy. Background Autopilot sessions and -p runs still decline requests that need
  manual MCP input.

Passwords for sudo, ssh and git:

  Commands the agent runs have no terminal, so sudo, ssh or git over HTTPS fails when it asks for
  a password. Run such a command yourself in the interactive shell that a lone $ opens.

  With experimental mode on (/settings experimental on or --experimental), the interactive CLI
  shows the prompt instead: type the answer, masked as you type, and press Enter, or Esc to
  cancel. Only the program that asked gets it; the agent never sees it. Not in autopilot or for
  sandboxed commands; on Windows only git and ssh ask.

Folder trust:

  When you start in a folder that is not trusted, Copilot asks:
    Yes                                                  Trust it for this session.
    Yes, and remember this folder for future sessions    Add it to `trustedFolders` in config.json.
    No                                                   Exit.
  Subfolders of a trusted folder are trusted. A -p run in an untrusted folder skips its workspace
  MCP servers and repository hooks; --trust-folder trusts the folder for that run only.
